text: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah, the daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Uzziah had done—except that he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people continued in their corrupt ways.
He rebuilt the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and he did extensive building on the wall of Ophel.
He also built cities in the hill country of Judah, and forts and towers in the wooded areas.

He went to war against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. That year the Ammonites paid him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand cors of barley. The Ammonites brought him the same tribute in the second and third years as well.

versions.text: He went to war against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. That year the Ammonites paid him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. They brought him the same tribute in the second and third years as well.
versions.explanation: Repeating "cors" makes the list clearer for a listener; "ten thousand of barley" leaves the unit hanging when read aloud. A footnote giving approximate modern equivalents for the talent and the cor would also help hearers grasp the size of the tribute.

versions.text: That year the Ammonites paid him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand cors of barley.
versions.explanation: Two whole clauses of the Hebrew have dropped out: the opening statement that Jotham warred against the king of the Ammonites and prevailed over them (וְהוּא נִלְחַם עִם־מֶלֶךְ בְּנֵי־עַמּוֹן וַיֶּחֱזַק עֲלֵיהֶם), and the closing note that they rendered the same tribute in the second and third years (זֹאת הֵשִׁיבוּ לוֹ בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן וּבַשָּׁנָה הַשֵּׁנִית וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁית). Without the first clause the tribute has no cause and 'That year' has no antecedent. The intentional repetition of 'cors' for oral clarity is retained.

text: So Jotham grew powerful, because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God.
The rest of the acts of Jotham, all his wars and all his ways, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

versions.text: The rest of the acts of Jotham, all his wars and all he undertook, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has וּדְרָכָיו, "and his ways," the same noun rendered "ways" in verse 6. "All he undertook" is a loose paraphrase and loses the deliberate verbal link with verse 6, where Jotham "ordered his ways." Keeping "ways" preserves the echo and reads just as smoothly aloud.

text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Then Jotham rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And his son Ahaz became king in his place.
